title: My father needs a lift. Should I rent a home, or buy one now?
shortTitle: A home with a lift for Dad
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #258 | SHOULD I GIVE UP IF I HAVE LOW INCOME?
excerpt: A 27-year-old engineer earning RM5,000 lives with his parents in a Penang walk-up, and his father now needs a wheelchair. Sean says rent a place with a lift now, and that his goal of three properties can wait.

qa.asker: Sam, a viewer from Penang who wrote in by email
qa.context: Sam is 27, an engineer earning RM5,000 a month, and lives with his parents in a walk-up public housing flat in Penang. His father's health has worsened and he now needs a wheelchair. Renting a home with a lift would cost RM1,000 to RM1,500 a month; buying would mean about RM400,000 or more on Penang Island, using up his loan eligibility. He had set himself Sean's goal of three properties.
qa.question: Should he rent a place with a lift, or buy one and give up his goal of owning three properties?
qa.quote: I think you should rent first
qa.answer: Rent a place with a lift now, since his father cannot wait for a purchase to complete, and rent out the walk-up to offset it. Put property investment aside until he has an emergency fund, insurance and more income; the three properties are meant to come about one a decade, not now.

reasons.title: Buying can't solve it quickly
reasons.body: A subsale takes five to six months and about 18% of the price in cash, around RM72,000 on RM400,000, plus RM20,000 to RM30,000 for renovation. A new launch takes three to four years. Renting works almost at once.

reasons.title: Three properties over 20 years
reasons.body: Sean's goal is one at about 28, one at 38 and one at 48, as income grows. Judging the future by today's salary undersells what a career can earn.

reasons.title: Investing needs three things first
reasons.body: Six months of expenses saved, covering the parents who depend on him; insurance for himself as the breadwinner; and a clear career path. Property is not a guaranteed win.

reasons.title: RM5,000 is not a low income
reasons.body: Sean says Sam earns about the average and should stop calling himself low-income. The better question is how to add RM500 or RM1,000 a month.

actions: Rent a unit with a lift for your father now.
Rent out the walk-up flat to cover part of the new rent.
Build six months of family expenses in savings and get insurance for yourself.
Find ways to earn an extra RM500 to RM1,000 a month from your professional skills.
Revisit buying once you have about RM100,000 set aside and a higher income.
qa.caveat: If he already had about RM100,000 in savings, buying an affordable subsale with a lift could make sense; Sean would not count a family home bought out of need as wasted loan eligibility.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #258. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as stated in August 2024.
